newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Mandela urges Singapore firms to invest in S.Africa.
newsitem.headline: Mandela urges Singapore firms to invest in S.Africa.

text.p: President Nelson Mandela on Wednesday urged more Singapore companies to invest in South Africa and share management and technical skills with his people.
Mandela, on a two-day visit to Singapore as part of a four-nation Asian tour, said South Africa adopted a new, investor-friendly macroeconomic strategy last year.

"This strategy includes fiscal discipline, human resource development and massive infrastructural programmes," he said at a dinner hosted by President Ong Teng Cheong. "For us, Singapore is an excellent partner in these endeavours."
Ong said Singapore was prepared to work with South Africa to develop its potential as a trade and tourism hub between East Asia and Southern Africa.
He said members of a business delegation that accompanied Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong on a recent visit to South Africa have already started working on potential joint ventures.
Ong said he was confident the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and the Southern African Development Community, of which Mandela is chairman, could work well together.

Mandela has said during his Asian tour that he wanted to deepen economic ties with ASEAN and learn how to raise the living conditions of his people from the region's own economic success. ASEAN comprises Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
Mandela, who has been to the Philippines and Brunei, also met Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew. He is due to leave for Malaysia on Thursday.
On his trip he has been accompanied by Graca Machel, widow of former Mozambique president Samora Machel and a 50-member delegation, including ministers and businessmen.
Mandela visited Singapore's Botanic Gardens, where an orchid was named after him and another was named after Machel.

Bilateral trade reached Singapore $945 million (US$665.5 million) in 1996, with Singapore's exports to South Africa comprising just over 65 percent of the total. South Africa is Singapore's largest economic partner in Africa.
